names.description: Only these columns. Null means every profiled and skipped column.

flagged_only.description: True keeps only columns that raised a flag. Null means false.

offset.description: How many matching columns to skip, for the next page. Null means 0. Constraints: at least 0.

limit.description: Most columns to return, from 1 to 15. Null means 15. Constraints: at least 1; at most 15.

output.description: One page of full column profiles. ``result.get(name)`` finds one column.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.
Position 4, `hint`: Library-written advice, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A capped list was cut. Call ``operation`` to read the rest. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.

total.description: How many columns match the filters.

offset.description: How many matching columns this page skipped.

columns.description: Matching columns: flagged ones first, then dataset order. At most 15; when more remain, ``omitted`` counts them and names ``describe_columns``.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `role`, `semantic_type`, `numeric_kind`, `dtype`, `parsed_dtype`, `type_flags`, `flags`, `cardinality`, `missingness`, `stats`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One column's full profile. No cell values. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name, exactly as in the data.
Position 1, `role`: ``target`` for a declared target, ``skipped`` for a column in ``skip_columns`` (no statistics), else ``feature``.
Position 2, `semantic_type`: Detected or declared semantic type; null when skipped.
Position 3, `numeric_kind`: ``continuous`` or ``bounded_discrete`` for a numeric column; else null.
Position 4, `dtype`: The column's storage type as loaded, such as ``Int64`` or ``String``.
Position 5, `parsed_dtype`: The storage type profiling read it as, after any coercion; null when skipped.
Position 6, `type_flags`: How the semantic type was decided, such as ``encoded_category`` or ``user_override``.
Position 7, `flags`: Flags raised on the column, each named ``<group>.<flag>``. ``flag_dials`` names the dials behind each.
Position 8, `cardinality`: Number of distinct non-missing values; null when skipped.
How much of one column is missing.

null_count.description: Rows missing, sentinels and blank strings included.

null_ratio.description: Share of rows missing, sentinels and blank strings included.

standard_null_count.description: Rows that were null in the file itself, before sentinels were read as missing.

severity.description: Missing-value severity, graded by the ``thresholds.missingness.severity_*`` dials of ``profile``; null when nothing is missing.

co_missing_with.description: Columns whose missing rows go with this column's, above ``thresholds.missingness.mar_correlation_threshold``. At most 10; ``missingness`` lists every pair.

anyOf.description: Position 9, `missingness`: How much is missing; null when skipped.
Statistics of a numeric column. No cell values: bounds and percentiles are in ``value_summary``.

skew_severity.description: Skew graded by the ``thresholds.numeric.skew_*`` dials of ``profile``.

kurtosis_tag.description: Kurtosis graded by the ``thresholds.numeric.kurt_*`` dials of ``profile``.

mode_share.description: Share of rows holding the most common value.

outlier_density.description: Share of values that are outliers, by ``thresholds.numeric.outlier_sigma_threshold``.

anyOf.description: Which tail of a numeric column holds more of its spread.

tag.description: ``right_heavy``, ``left_heavy`` or ``symmetric``, graded by the ``thresholds.numeric.tail_asymmetry_*`` dials of ``profile``.

right_share.description: Share of the spread beyond the median that lies in the right tail.

tails.description: Tail asymmetry; null when not measured.

anyOf.description: The bimodality test readings of a numeric column.

dip_p_value.description: The dip test's p-value. Low means more than one mode.

separation.description: Separation between the two modes (Ashman's D).

minority_weight.description: Share of rows in the smaller mode.

bimodal.description: Bimodality test readings; null when the column was not tested further.

anyOf.description: How a numeric column relates to the other numeric columns. Routing reads these.

tag.description: The relationship, graded by the ``thresholds.nonlinearity`` dials of ``profile``.

spearman_pearson_discrepancy.description: Largest Spearman-minus-Pearson gap over the other numeric columns.

mean_mutual_information.description: Mean excess mutual information with the other numeric columns, in nats.

max_mutual_information.description: Largest mutual information with another numeric column, in nats.

r2_linear.description: R² of a linear model predicting this column from the others.

r2_rf.description: R² of a random forest predicting this column from the others.

heteroscedasticity_p_value.description: Breusch-Pagan p-value of the linear model's residuals. Low means uneven spread.

nonlinearity.description: Nonlinearity probe readings; null when the column was not probed.

anyOf.description: Statistics of a categorical column. No labels: they are in ``value_summary``.

mode_share.description: Share of rows holding the most common label.

rare_row_share.description: Share of rows holding one of those rare labels.

stratification_rare_label_count.description: Labels rarer than ``thresholds.categorical.stratification_rare_threshold_pct``, which a stratified split protects.

dominant_class_ratio.description: Count of the most common label divided by the second most common.

normalized_entropy.description: Shannon entropy of the labels, from 0 (one label) to 1 (all equally common).

normalized_gini.description: Gini impurity of the labels, from 0 (one label) to 1 (all equally common).

anyOf.description: Statistics of a datetime column. The first and last dates are in ``value_summary``.

range_days.description: Days from the first date to the last.

median_gap_seconds.description: Median gap between consecutive dates, in seconds.

gap_cv.description: Coefficient of variation of the gaps between dates.

future_date_count.description: Dates after the time of profiling.

anyOf.description: Statistics of a boolean column.

true_share.description: Share of non-missing rows holding true.

anyOf.description: Statistics of a free-text column.

empty_share.description: Share of values that are empty.

whitespace_share.description: Share of values that are only whitespace.

anyOf.description: Position 10, `stats`: Statistics for the column's semantic type, told apart by ``kind``; null when skipped, for an identifier, or when profiling failed.

flag_dials.description: One entry per flag raised on a column of this page, in ``columns`` order of first appearance.

fields.description: Always exactly `flag`, `dials`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: The dials that decide one flag. Turn one to change which columns raise the flag. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `flag`: The flag, as in ``columns[].flags``.
Position 1, `dials`: Every dial the flag's rule reads, with its resolved value. Empty when no dial decides it, as for ``missingness.fully_null``.

fields.description: Always exactly `operation`, `dial`, `value`, `source`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: The dial whose value decided a threshold outcome. Turn it to change the outcome. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `operation`: The Operation that takes the dial.
Position 1, `dial`: The dial's argument path, such as ``thresholds.missingness.high_null_ratio``.
Position 2, `value`: The dial's resolved value.
Position 3, `source`: ``default`` when the library default decided, ``argument`` when the caller set it.
